sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified 1915 Companies Law, Napoleonic/French legal tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg is covered by the bilateral investment treaties (BITs) concluded by the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU); active examples include the BLEU-China BIT (1984) and the BLEU-Hong Kong SAR BIT.

Luxembourg maintains a broad double-taxation treaty (DTAA) network, including current treaties with the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, the Netherlands and the People's Republic of China.
EU free-movement and free-capital rights under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Regulation (EU) 2019/452 apply within the internal market.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal implementing regulations; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF Regulations and Circulars (including CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 20/744)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or commercial register extract of every corporate general partner and limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, US Secretary of State, German Handelsregister)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for HCCH member jurisdictions) or Luxembourg Consular Legalization (non-member jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / existence certificate for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court, chamber of commerce or public registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing Luxembourg counsel and/or the Luxembourg domiciliation agent to execute the formation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution of the POA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Luxembourg Consular Legalization; if signed before a Luxembourg notary, notarization alone is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residence addresses of all ultimate beneficial owners and natural-person signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State passport office / municipal or registrar office in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, with apostille/consular legalization if required by the Luxembourg AML obliged professional

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Organisation chart / shareholder structure identifying all beneficial owners above the 25% threshold and the source of funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate parent company or Luxembourg legal counsel preparing the pre-incorporation due-diligence file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certification by a Luxembourg 'professionnel' subject to the 2004 AML/CFT Law; no apostille where executed in Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory: (1) screening of all UBOs, directors, authorised signatories and beneficial owners against PEP databases as defined in Art. 3(1)(28) of the AML/CFT Law; (2) screening against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council asset-freeze lists, Luxembourg national sanctions listings and OFAC SDN/Consolidated list due to USD-based AdMob/AppLovin payment rails; (3) FATF high-risk country checks and enhanced due diligence for PEPs or higher-risk jurisdictions; (4) adverse media and negative-news monitoring before onboarding; (5) full file approval by the Luxembourg notary/law firm/domiciliation agent as an AML obliged entity before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory corporate documents and RCS filings must be in French, German or Luxembourgish; the corporate name must be in Latin script. Non-Latin-script commercial names may be used only as a transliteration/an alias in the RCS, and the legal name in the notarial deed must be Latin-script and distinguishable from prior RCS entries.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / banking (requires CSSF banking licence)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance (requires insurance authority authorisation)
SICAV / SICAF / FCP / Fonds / Fund (regulated investment-vehicle tokens)
État / National / Royal / Commune (public or sovereign connotations)
Chambre de Commerce (statutorily protected chamber denomination)
The suffix 'SCSp' is mandatory for the SCSp corporate-form identifier; it is not a prohibited token
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name, the RCS/LBR issues a written refusal. Within 10 business days the notary may (a) submit up to three alternative names, or (b) file an appeal before the Chambre Commerciale of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg under the company-law name-clearance rules. The appeal must be accompanied by the refusal notice, a due-diligence report on RCS conflicts, the draft partnership deed, and a legal memorandum in French. Extensions of the initial 30-day reservation may be requested at least 5 working days before expiry; extensions are discretionary, non-statutory and depend on LBR policy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only where the Luxembourg registered office is held through an authorised corporate domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation. The virtual office may be treated as sufficient for registry registration, but actual substance (bank account, minimal management, records, and control) must be verifiable for AML/CFT and tax treaty purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg authorities for a passive SCSp with a standard domiciliation agent. The probability rises to 20-25% if the RCS/law enforcement is notified of anomalous substance, foreign management of a Luxembourg-registered SCSp, or tax-driven restructuring indications.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS/LBR name-search and availability clearance for the SCSp name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative tariff per LBR price list; non-refundable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of constitution (acte de société) for the SCSp, including drafting, partner consent and legalisation of corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market notarial scale of EUR 2,000 – EUR 4,000 for a standard SCSp formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official publication filing fees and RCS fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE / beneficial-owner register filing (initial declaration of UBOs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal administrative fee for online RBE registration and digital acknowledgment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and SCSp domiciliation service (first year, paid in advance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 2,500 – EUR 3,500 per annum for a non-financial SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC, PEP and sanctions screening package for UBOs, directors and authorised representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per UBO and per corporate entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and/or consular legalization of the foreign corporate documentation bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notaries, apostille authorities and Luxembourg consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-document tariffs, courier and translation costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg legal fees for pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting the partnership agreement and filing review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly rate EUR 450 – EUR 700 or fixed fee for standard SCSp formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for name appeal, translation or corrective/refilings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg court registry, certificate translators and RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency buffer of 10% on official fees and professional fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 944-1 to 944-26 (Société en Commandite Spéciale); residual provisions of the Civil Code on partnership contracts
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership agreement (contrat de société) filed electronically via the Luxembourg electronic filing platform (RBE), together with the registration application
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None; the SCSp has no minimum statutory capital and no escrow or paid-up capital is required. Capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement. In-kind contributions require an inventory unless the contribution is real estate, in which case a notarial deed is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the proposed Special Limited Partnership agreement of LU SCSP is approved and adopted as the governing charter; that the initial capital contributions and subscriptions of the limited partners are accepted; that the registered office located at 1, rue du Parc, L-1234 Luxembourg is ratified as the partnership’s statutory seat; that [Name] is appointed sole manager and authorised signatory of the general partner; that the general partner is instructed to execute all filings before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, the publication in the RESA, and any other registration required; and that this resolution shall be effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online portal (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the requested partnership name against the Trade and Companies Register and, if necessary, reserve the name through the RBE portal. This prevents conflict with a prior registered entity and verifies the availability of the SCSp name. For a special limited partnership with no legal personlity, the statutory name of the general partner or of a designated branch may appear.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name
Identification documents of the general partner
Identification documents of the limited partner(s)
Proof of address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to identity or confusion with an existing entity, submit a revised name or obtain a letter of no objection from the conflicting registered owner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and limited partners, with optional assistance of a Luxembourg notary or lawyer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement containing the firm name, duration, registered office in Luxembourg, object, capital and share of profits, contribution of each partner, the identity of the general partner and the limited partners, and governance rules. The agreement may be executed by private deed; notarisation is mandatory only if an immovable asset is contributed or if public capital-raising is contemplated.
required_dossiers: Notarised or private-deed partnership agreement
Contributions schedule and subscription letter
Identity/address documents of all partners
Act of appointment of the general partner (if a corporate entity)
Bank certificate of contribution release (if cash contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS refuses the agreement because of missing legal formalities, correct the offending clauses, re-execute the signatures, and resubmit within the cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration in the Trade and Companies Register and publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS via the RBE portal; publication is made in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the RBE portal with a LuxTrust qualified electronic signature, complete the RCS registration form, upload the signed partnership agreement and supporting documents, and pay the filing fee. The RCS will register the SCSp and send the file for publication in the RESA. The publication must occur within one month of the first public appearance of the partnership.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic RCS application form
Executed partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address
Consent of the general partner to act as manager
Qualified electronic signature (LuxTrust) of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a notice of rejection or a formal query, submit the requested evidence or amendments via the RBE within the statutory cure period. If the RCS maintains a refusal, the general partner may appeal to the Luxembourg tribunal d’arrondissement within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes), Registration Duties, VAT and Excise Authority (AEDT), Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, register the SCSp for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax if applicable. If the SCSp is treated as transparent for Luxembourg tax purposes, the partners report their distributive share; nevertheless, registration for VAT is required if the activity exceeds the VAT threshold or engages in taxable supplies. The manager must also register employers with the CCSS for any employees.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait) with file number
Tax filing form 1002 or 1002bis
VAT registration form if required
Identity and EORI numbers of partners
Employer registration form for social security
Lease contract confirming the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration requests additional documents or deems the registration incomplete, file the missing schedules online within the indicated deadline and request a taxable status confirmation or advance tax ruling if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational setup and office/IT compliance clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Communal administration (mairie) of the city of the registered office, Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS), Ministry of Labour / ITM (Inspection du Travail et des Mines)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the lease for the registered office and ensure the premises satisfy fire safety and occupational health standards. For a hyper-casual mobile-games publishing company, no industrial or manufacturing licence is required, but the office space must have a fire evacuation certificate, electrical installation conformity, and a valid building occupancy permit. If the company hosts gaming servers, verify structural load capacity and environmental limitations for cooling and electricity.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement
Fire safety certificate for the office premises
Electrical installation certificate / building conformity document
IT and internet service provider contract
Data protection register (GDPR) if processing user data
Insurance policy covering professional liability and office contents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal fire or ITM inspection reports non-compliance, execute corrective works, re-inspection, and obtain the final clearance certificate before employees commence activities at the premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing authority applicable; the activity is a digitised publishing and software-development service performed in an office environment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit required; the SCSp only needs the RCS registration and standard office-related municipal clearances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development (MECSD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 0 – Non-industrial office use; no formal EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater discharge, combustion emissions or hazardous waste generation. Standard municipal waste-collection obligations apply; expired electronic equipment must be handled pursuant to the EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU through a licensed recycler; paper waste is separated and recycled.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval is required from the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office and any server/storage area, including signage, escape routes and extinguishers. The building must have a valid structural load certificate where racked IT equipment is installed. Occupational clearance is issued by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM) covering lighting, ergonomics, ventilation and access to welfare facilities. For a low-risk office activity, these clearances are obtained through a declaration and a visual inspection by the relevant authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - direct income tax; e-portal: myGuichet.lu / guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned SCSp must first be registered with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and obtain a national identification number (matricule). For VAT purposes, the entity or its tax representative must submit a registration application to the AEDT on form 864A, either in paper or via the myGuichet portal. Direct tax registration is achieved through the competent Luxembourg business tax office (bureau d'imposition), which opens a corporate tax file for the partnership. Non-established foreign entities with no permanent establishment in Luxembourg may register for VAT directly via the AEDT or use the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) mechanism for EU cross-border electronic services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) Articles 4bis and 175; no check-the-box election is available. Partners are taxable on their distributive share. For hybrid mismatch purposes, elections may be available under ATAD (EU Directive 2016/1164) to align treatment with a foreign jurisdiction. The SCSp may elect to have a permanent establishment or taxable presence under certain double tax treaties, but cannot be treated as a fully taxable entity for Luxembourg corporate income tax unless it is converted to a different corporate form. VAT has no transparency election; the SCSp is a taxable person where it supplies taxable services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold for small-enterprise exemption (Art. 57 Loi TVA); no general registration threshold for established taxable persons. Non-established suppliers must register from the first euro of taxable supply in Luxembourg unless OSS (One-Stop-Shop) is used. For cross-border distance sales of goods and B2C electronic services to other EU Member States, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual turnover threshold applies (Art. 42 Loi TVA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no government digital stamping or continuous transaction controls. E-invoicing is permitted subject to authenticity of origin and integrity of content. Mandatory SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) reporting applies for VAT audits. Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals, mandatory B2B e-invoicing is planned with implementation expected no earlier than 2025-2027. The OSS (One-Stop-Shop) VAT electronic filing portal is integrated via myGuichet.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT is applied to exports of physical goods to non-EU destinations provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of supply and documentary evidence of export is retained. Services: B2B supplies of electronic services (including hyper-casual ad-monetized games) to a non-EU customer are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (zero-rated) when the customer is a taxable person established in a non-EU country; B2C supplies to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of VAT under the place-of-supply rules. Intra-EU B2B supplies may be zero-rated in Luxembourg via OSS where the recipient supplies a valid EU VAT identification number. Export-related input VAT claims require proper invoices and export documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/IE-507 or electronic ECS declaration)
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Airway Bill (for physical goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT payment evidence (for offshore proceeds)
Evidence of non-EU customer status (foreign VAT ID, residency certificate, or self-declaration)
AdMob/AppLovin payout reports and IP/location logs substantiating destination of electronic services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may impose penalties of up to 10% of the suppressed VAT amount for late payments, increasing to 20% where there is intent to evade or attempt to evade VAT (Art. 26 Loi TVA). Fraudulent export zero-rating claims trigger retrospective VAT assessments, automatic interest, and clawback of input VAT credits. Criminal prosecution for VAT fraud can result in fines of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment for the persons involved. The statute of limitations for VAT clawback is 5 years; it extends to 10 years where the taxpayer has acted in bad faith.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), established under Article 2 of the Law of 22 April 1998, acting together with the Ministère des Finances for exchange control and payments-system oversight; prudential regulation and AML/CTF supervision of regulated financial institutions are delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the CSSF's AML/CTF unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full liberalisation under OECD capital-movement instruments and EU Treaty rules on free movement of capital and payments. There is no distinction between current account and capital account convertibility for commercial purposes, no exchange control or Moratorium, and no BCL licensing/approval gate for profits or dividends remittances. In practice, partners of an SCSp can freely convert EUR to FX and repatriate profit allocations directly to foreign investors; the only substantive hurdles are tax compliance (CRS/CBCF declarations, withholding on non-resident corporate partners only if treaty-protected exemptions are unavailable) and the bank's internal KYC-risk screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. Receipts from advertising payouts, royalties, or game publishing exports may be held indefinitely in foreign currency accounts without mandatory conversion to EUR. Enterprises only need to report cross-border transactions for balance-of-payments statistics under BCL statistical thresholds (monthly/quarterly OECD and EU balance-of-payments reporting), with zero conversion ratio.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury custody and clearing, Medium as an auxiliary receivables-collection gateway. An EEA e-money institution (EMI) authorised in another Member State can passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and settle EUR/SEPA flows, but cannot provide fiduciary-grade core treasury services for an SCSp without credit-institution backing. A non-EEA/offshore EMI has no autonomous passporting right; any bank-like activity in Luxembourg requires a CSSF e-money or payment institution licence under the Law of 10 June 2009 and is operationally impractical for a cash-rich gaming treasury. Therefore, the SCSp should use Luxembourg domiciled credit institutions for liquidity and hedge execution, and may restrict EMIs to collections aggregators.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In standard Luxembourg banking practice, at least one signatory/representative of the SCSp's management company or general partner must appear physically at the bank's registered office or secure outpost for signature verification, especially where non-resident investors or a purely foreign management structure exist. Remote opening via video-identification is generally accepted for non-licensed low-risk partnerships, subject to CSSF AML/CTF circular-letter conditions, but the bank's internal KYC policy often still requires a physical-once meeting for final account activation. The most robust structure is to appoint a Luxembourg-based resident corporate general partner (SCS, SARL, or a local professional administrator) whose bodies attend in person, supported by apostilled corporate documents, UBO identification, and ad-network contract evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume microtransactions from foreign ad networks (AdMob/AppLovin) without a clean contractual chain causing money-laundering ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed publisher/developers agreements with Google Ireland Ltd and AppLovin Corp; ad-network consolidated settlement statements and payout history; audited monthly revenue reports; user-acquisition campaign invoices; Apple/Google developer-console screenshots with app identifiers; ISIC/NAICS classification certificate explaining the hyper-casual ad-monetization model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through taxation with non-resident partners unregistered in ultimate-beneficial-owner filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg CUR/BEN registers (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) confirmation receipt; extensive UBO file with passports, utility bills, corporate org charts; partnership agreement and management-mandate instrument; written confirmation of TIE between partners and SCSp; Swiss/US/EU tax residence certificates for all investors above 25% threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP royalties and licensing payments to/from the SCSp to foreign development studios presenting as transfer-pricing abuse
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP ownership chain documentation containing registered copyright/trademark or assignment agreements; licence and sub-licence contracts with arm's-length amounts; OECD transfer-pricing documentation including functional and country-risk analysis; external valuations and commissionaire file; commercial invoices matching payment templates; business-substance file showing actual constant monitoring of licensed assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to software/data-advertising partners domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy on jurisdiction sanction screening (EU, OFAC, UN lists); evidentiary file of CDD/KYC for all counterparties with ownership and licence details; supplier contractual terms with service descriptions; transaction-level executive summary demonstrating actual gaming-ad infrastructure needs; bank-required source-of-funds statement and negative media screening from Reuters/Dow Jones.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Investor capital contributions into the SCSp should be routed via SWIFT MT103 (single high-value line) from each partner's bank account to the account held at a Luxembourg credit institution, using the payment purpose code 'P5201 – Equity and investment fund shares of an investment fund' or 'P5710 – Capital transfers within EU' as applicable. For large SCA transactions in USD/EUR above EUR 1,000,000, an MT103 with SWIFT cover TRN and direct correspondent instructions is advised; transfers must mention the SCSp's full legal name, investor reference, and cross-reference to the subscription agreement / partnership deed. The receiving bank requires a CSSF-compliant BOI declaration (UBO register), a capital contribution statement from the partnership deed, and a no-AML block verification; no BCL licence is required for inward capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-liability settlements for the hyper-casual games treasury will primarily clear over SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA counterparties (e.g., US, UK, APAC ad networks and marketing agencies) and via SEPA Instant/SEPA CT for intra-EEA publishers/influencers. For high-value development-financing / co-publishing agreements where the SCSp issues a purchase order or a material services commitment, a confirmed irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (Commercial LC) issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank can be used as a banker's acceptance; more commonly payments will be launched through the bank's host-to-host cash-management portal with batch-payment files. USD liquidity should be held in a segregated Nostro/USD clearing account to be converted only against a real settlement or hedging transaction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD FX forward contracts (vanilla deliverable forwards) offered by the Luxembourg credit institution under EMIR/MiFID II
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic/illiquid currencies received from advertisement networks, to be transacted only with CSSF/ECB-licensed EU banks
Cross-currency swap agreements (IRS/CCS) between SCSp and LUX-licensed derivative counterparties for fixed-to-floating EUR/USD treasury duration alignment
FX vanilla options purchased from EU multicurrency settlement platforms as asymmetry-protection overlays

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation of registration particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following each anniversary date of initial RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 250–1,000 per missed confirmation; repeated failure triggers formal notice and potential administrative strike-off from RCSL after court referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following each anniversary date of RBE registration; any change in UBOs also must be filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 950 to EUR 12,500 per violation; criminal penalties up to EUR 50,000 and/or six months imprisonment for deliberate non-compliance; potential freeze of dividend distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax return (pass-through declaration of allocable income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority, ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Statutory deadline 31 May of the year following the tax year; online filing via MyGuichet.lu automatically extends to 31 December of that year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10%–50% of assessed tax; default interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid taxes; forced assessment by tax office and criminal fine up to EUR 5,000 for intentional omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts publication (only if SCSp is not exempt; typically exempt for SCSp under commercial law)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCSL/Luxembourg Official Gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If applicable, within six months of financial year-end, with public filing no later than 30 days after approval by partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For non-exempt entities: fines of EUR 500–2,000 and forced publication by court order; SCSp generally statutorily exempt from annual accounts publication, so no practical sanction applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SCSp must undergo a statutory independent audit if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 7.4 million; net turnover above EUR 15 million; average workforce above 50 employees. However, SCSp vehicles are typically exempt from audit unless the partnership agreement expressly requires it or a corporate general partner is subject to mandatory audit under group thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (PCN – Plan comptable normalisé) under the Law of 19 December 2002, as amended; voluntary adoption of IFRS as endorsed by the EU if the SCSp is listed or forms part of a consolidated group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the SCSp's general partner (manager) must confirm, through the RBE online portal, that all beneficial owners are correctly listed and that any shareholding or partnership-interest transfers executed during the year have been previously updated. The annual confirmation is separate from change-triggered filings and must be submitted even if no ownership movement occurred.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Partners (Register des associés)
Minute Book of partner and management decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 (exempt) – USD 25,000 for voluntary or threshold-triggered audit per year

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City CIT rate (17% base corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent and as such is generally not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax; income is allocated to partners. Eligible taxpayers may benefit from the Luxembourg IP regime (80% exemption), investment tax credit, and participation exemption. If an optional transparent entity opts into corporate taxability or a partner is a Luxembourg resident corporate partner, the statutory aggregate rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 700 (annual corporate income tax return) filed via MyGuichet.lu / Cooperative e-Tax system; partnerships may also file Annex 500 for fiscal transparency reporting
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the end of the financial year, with extension possibilities for electronic filing; if the FYE is 31 December, the filing is due by 31 May of the following year unless extension is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification, registered office, RCS number and tax file number (matricule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partner details must be listed on the tax return if the SCSp is filing as transparent; no partner-level profit allocation is reported by the entity to Luxembourg unless loss/income attribution requires recognition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing balance sheet amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special adjustment required for non-resident partners; foreign assets or transfers to a Luxembourg partnership are reported at the entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable basis calculation before loss relief and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For transparent SCSp, net taxable income is nil at entity level; the actual allocation to each non-resident partner follows national allocation rules and may be subject to Luxembourg withholding at the partnership level when the partner is not treaty-protected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year losses offset against current-year income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward is available to Luxembourg-resident corporate partners under rules; non-resident partners can only apply losses through their home jurisdiction, subject to treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to intercompany pricing to align with arm's length standard
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments between SCSp and non-resident affiliates require contemporaneous documentation if above TP threshold; entry must reflect final arm’s length position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing causes penalties between EUR 50 and EUR 2,500 per return (or 10% of unpaid tax in severe cases) plus late payment interest at 7.2% per annum (0.6% per month) accruing on the assessed net liability; intentional omission may trigger criminal tax penalties up to EUR 500,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax on distributions by Luxembourg resident companies; 0% for SCSp distributions because SCSp is transparent and not a taxable distribution company; reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or treaty where a qualified corporate partner holds at least 10% stake for 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a signed tax residency certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, a Form 2B/declaration of partial exemption, and evidence of full beneficial ownership. The Luxembourg withholding agent or tax administration reviews the DTA limitation-on-benefits clause (where present) and the EU anti-abuse test. For SCSp, treaty entitlement is tested at the partner level because Luxembourg looks through the partnership where the partner is resident in a treaty state and subject to tax on allocated profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding tax 15% (reduced under EU Interest & Royalty Directive to 0% for related EU companies and under treaties to 0-5%). Interest: no general Luxembourg withholding tax on arm's length interest paid to non-residents; 0% under EU Directive for qualifying associated enterprises.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 5,000,000 aggregated value of controlled transactions or group consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750,000,000 triggers Master File and Local File compilation; in practice, Luxembourg tax audit requires TP documentation from the first euro when intercompany transactions pose significant tax risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Requirements through the OECD/MLI and the Anti-Abuse provisions (DAC6, CFC, GAAR). A SCSp with no asset, risk, or personnel in Luxembourg cannot claim treaty benefits arising from Luxembourg; management, adequate premises, decision-making and accounting functions must be present in Luxembourg or in the state entitled to treaty benefits. The EU Directive (ATAD) requires substantive economic activity to be evidenced where a paper entity receives interest, royalties, or dividend income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of taxable income, fraudulent invoices, or misreporting of revenues and losses in the SCSp
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to EUR 500,000 plus 10% to 80% of the evaded tax; tax authorities may also impose a fine equal to 3 times the evaded tax in the gravest cases (Article 215 LIR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for corporate tax debts if they knowingly filed inaccurate returns or used the SCSp as a vehicle to conceal personal assets; criminal prosecution can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp lacking economic substance, personnel, business premises, or bank accounts used solely to channel royalties, dividends, or interest from hyper-casual mobile gaming revenue without real local activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; reclassification of transferred profits as constructive dividends or deemed taxable income; administration fines and invalidation of intra-group agreements; for letterbox companies, liquidation orders and revocation of Luxembourg residence status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to personal civil restitution for unwound transactions, travel bans, freezing of assets, and disqualification as directors for up to 10 years; criminal liability where the artificial structure is proven fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to register the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) of the SCSp in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) or failing to maintain accurate records of partners behind the hyper-casual gaming payout flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 100,000 or 5% of turnover; criminal sanction up to EUR 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years for systematic breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid fines and any damages caused to creditors or minority partners; the court may prohibit the director from exercising commercial activity for up to 15 years.
